persona.goal: drop narrowband AND generally bad-sounding audio
persona.opening_prompt: I want to weed out the low-quality audio - both the tinny, telephone-sounding stuff and anything that just sounds bad overall.
persona.persona_facts: Mix of narrowband (telephone) and wideband clips.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.text: I want to weed out the low-quality audio - both the tinny, telephone-sounding stuff and anything that just sounds bad overall.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
I now have what I need to plan. Here's what I found in the catalog:

- **"Tinny, telephone-sounding"** → this is **narrowband/telephony** audio. `BandFilterStage` (a cheap CPU classifier) does exactly this: `band_value: full_band` keeps hi-fi wideband and drops telephony-style narrowband. This part of your request is unambiguous, so I'll handle it that way.
- **"Sounds bad overall"** → this is an **overall perceptual-quality** gate. The best fit is `UTMOSFilterStage`, which predicts a single overall MOS (0–5) — it maps cleanly to "overall quality" and is lighter than the alternative. (The alternative, `SIGMOSFilterStage`, breaks quality into 7 dimensions like noise/reverb/coloration; it's finer-grained and more aggressive, better suited to detailed TTS curation than a general "sounds bad" cull. I'd recommend UTMOS unless you specifically want per-dimension control.)

The one thing I genuinely can't infer is the **overall-quality bar** — and it's material because it drives how much audio gets dropped. "Weed out the bad" could mean any of three very different yields, and I won't hand-pick a threshold for a fuzzy word like "sounds bad." So one question before I build the recipe:

**How strict should the overall-quality cull be? Roughly:**
- **Lenient** — only drop the clearly-bad clips, keep as much as possible (maximum retention);
- **General** — a solid "good enough" bar for typical ASR/general use;
- **Studio** — keep only pristine, high-fidelity clips (drops a lot).

(The tinny/telephone removal happens either way — this question is only about the "sounds bad overall" part.) Once you pick a level, I'll `resolve` it to the concrete threshold, `validate` the recipe, and hand you the runnable pipeline.

card.summary: Predict UTMOS mean-opinion-score (MOS) and filter/annotate audio by quality.

resource.throughput_hint: fast on GPU; CPU fallback is slower

good_for: gate speech clips by overall perceptual quality

params_of_note.mos_threshold: minimum MOS to keep (0-5). TTS: >=4.0; ASR/general: >=3.4; max retention: >=2.5
params_of_note.action: 'filter' drops below threshold; 'annotate' keeps all and only writes the score

comparison.accuracy_hint: single overall MOS predictor; coarser than SIGMOS's 7 dimensions
comparison.known_limitations: predictor of human MOS, not a ground-truth measurement; speech-only

caveats: Downloads the model from torch.hub on first run (needs network once).
Score is a predictor of human MOS, not a ground-truth measurement.

params.name: mos_threshold
params.description: Minimum MOS score to pass (None to disable)

params.name: sample_rate
params.description: Target sample rate for UTMOS inference (default 16000)

params.name: input_residency
params.description: Which input to use — "waveform" (in-memory only), "file" (audio_filepath only), or "auto" (waveform first, file fallback; default).

params.name: mode
params.description: Where to score — "task" (top-level audio), "segments" (nested segments list), or "auto" (segments when segments_key is present, else task; default). Setting "task" or "segments" overrides the auto-detection.

params.name: action
params.description: "filter" drops items below mos_threshold; "annotate" keeps every item — including items that fail or cannot be scored — and only writes score_key.

params.description: Key where the UTMOS MOS score is written.
